title: Calibration of a prediction model: slope, calibration-in-the-large and O/E
summary: External validation of a published model's calibration: the calibration slope, the intercept with the slope fixed at 1, and the observed-to-expected ratio.

sizing._why: Validation sample size is set by the precision of the calibration slope and O/E (Riley et al. 2021); no catalog form takes it.

pinned_defaults: Calibration slope: coefficient of the linear predictor in glm(y ~ lp).
Calibration-in-the-large: intercept of glm(y ~ offset(lp)), slope fixed at 1; not the intercept of the slope model.
O/E: events over the sum of predicted risks. SEs written out as inverse information (statsmodels' IRLS covariance differed from R's vcov by 1e-6).
The calibration curve should be plotted but is not a harness key: R's loess and Python's lowess are different smoothers.
_truth: The published model's coefficients are 1.5 times too large and its intercept too high, so the true slope is exactly 2/3 and the model over-predicts on average.
